world.doc: The world board: how a march is timed and what an explorer sees (Docs/features/19-world-map.md §3–§4).

explorerSecondsPerHex.doc: Seconds an explorer takes to leave a hex of open ground; each hex multiplies it by its terrain and features (worldTravel), and worldRevealSpeed divides it.

armySecondsPerHex.doc: Seconds an army takes to leave a hex of open ground; each hex multiplies it by its terrain and features (worldTravel).

exploreWorkSeconds.doc: Seconds an explorer works at the hex it was sent to before it is revealed, whatever the distance.

exploreWorkSecondsPerHex.doc: Seconds more of that work for every hex the target lies from the city.

exploreGoldBase.doc: Gold to send an explorer to a hex next to the city.

exploreGoldGrowth.doc: How much dearer exploring is for every hex further from the city.

explorerRevealRadius.doc: Hexes round every hex of its path that a marching explorer reveals, before the tree.

revealRadiusMax.doc: The most a reveal radius can reach, however the tree raises it.

cartographyExplorers.doc: Explorer slots Cartography opens. The Atlas ladder adds to it.

rivals.doc: Who holds the five other cities until the board comes from the server.

armySlots.doc: Armies a player can have out from the moment the world opens; the War Camp adds one per level.

worldGen.doc: How a board is rolled (19 §9): one wedge, turned six times; the inner ring authored.

innerRing.doc: The six hexes round the Portal, east first and on round the compass. Authored, never rolled or turned.

terrainWeights.doc: The odds of each terrain, by the ring a hex is on. Relative weights.

home.doc: Ring 4, round the cities. A city hex itself is always Grassland.

featureChance.doc: The chance a hex rolls each feature, by its ring. Dungeons and Sanctuaries only on the outer ring; landmarks only on the corridors.

excludes.doc: The features it never shares a hex with. Both sides name each other.

featureRules.doc: Where each feature may roll, and what it never shares a hex with (Docs/plans/world-hex-art.md §1). A feature that does not fit is skipped; the inner ring must obey them too.

placedPerWedge.doc: Sites PLACED rather than rolled: exactly this many on the outer ring of every sixth of the board, never beside a city (19 §9). A placed feature has no chance of its own.

maxFeaturesPerHex.doc: A rolled hex keeps at most this many features, in the order they are listed.

worldBuild.doc: What is built on a held world hex and what it pays (Docs/features/19-world-map.md §5.1, §7).

claim.doc: Claiming a neutral hex: building its district. Takes a builder.

goldGrowth.doc: Each claim costs this many times the last, by hexes already held.

buildSeconds.doc: Seconds a builder spends on a district.

districts.doc: Each district: the feature that decides it, and what it pays. One per hex, the claim itself.

feature.doc: The feature a hex holds for this to be its district; None for bare ground.

produces.doc: The currency its store fills with; empty for one that makes nothing (the Shrine raises max Mana instead).

perHour.doc: What it adds to its store an hour, while its hex is active. The Rural district’s is a tenth of a full level-1 House.

store.doc: The most its store holds; a full store stops it.

upgrades.doc: What can be built into a district that stands, on any district.

buildSeconds.doc: Seconds a builder spends on it.

anyPrecious.doc: Precious material of any kind this level costs (19 §7.6).

goods.doc: Goods — precious materials, chiefly — this level costs.

innerRingMultiplier.doc: What a district on the inner ring makes and holds, times its rate (3 = +200%).

sanctuaryManaCap.doc: Max Mana each held, active Shrine adds.

worldBots.doc: The stand-in rivals of the local world server, until real players sit in the other five cities.

actEveryHours.doc: On average, how often a rival makes a move.

maxHexes.doc: The most hexes a rival ever claims; what it takes in a fight comes on top.

attackChance.doc: The chance a rival’s move is an attack on a neighbour’s ground beside its own.

armyPower.doc: What a rival’s attacking army is worth.

garrisonPower.doc: What a rival’s Fortress garrison is worth.

worldDungeon.doc: A dungeon: depths of rooms, a race — the first to clear its last boss closes it for everyone, and it comes back elsewhere in its sixth of the board (Docs/features/19-world-map.md §8.1, 11-expeditions.md).

roomsPerDepth.doc: Rooms in a depth; the last is its boss.

powerStart.doc: What room 1 of each depth fields.

powerStep.doc: What each room after the first adds, per depth.

bossMultiplier.doc: A boss fields this many times the room before it would.

rewardBase.doc: The reward scale of each depth.

rewardGrowth.doc: Each room pays this many times the one before it.

gold.doc: Gold a room pays, times the depth’s scale.

heroXp.doc: Hero XP a room pays, times the depth’s scale.

stardust.doc: Stardust a room pays, times the depth’s scale.

knowledge.doc: Knowledge a room pays, times the depth’s scale — at least 1.

bossRewardMultiplier.doc: A boss pays this many times a room.

closeRewardMultiplier.doc: Closing a dungeon pays its last boss again, this many times over, to whoever closed it.

returnHoursMin.doc: After a dungeon closes, it comes back after at least this many hours…

returnHoursMax.doc: …and at most this many: each return rolls a time between the two.

precious.doc: Precious material a room pays, by the same scale as its other rewards (19 §7.4) — mostly the player’s own.

nameFirst.doc: A dungeon’s name is “The <first> <second>”, rolled when it appears.

nameSecond.doc: The second word of a dungeon’s name.

bossNames.doc: Who waits at the bottom of each depth, rolled per dungeon and depth.

worldPortal.doc: The Dark Portal: a weekly depth ladder on the centre hex (Docs/features/19-world-map.md §10).

openWeekday.doc: The UTC weekday it opens on, 0 = Sunday. Always the same one.

openDays.doc: Days it stays open; it is shut the rest of the week.

attemptsPerDay.doc: Floors a player may clear a UTC day. A failed fight spends nothing.

powerGrowth.doc: Each floor fields this many times the one above.

rewardBase.doc: The reward scale of the first floor, on the dungeon room formula.

rewardGrowth.doc: Each floor pays this many times the one above.

roseEvery.doc: A Rose pack on every floor this many deep.

goldenEvery.doc: A Golden pack instead on every floor this many deep.

milestoneEvery.doc: A milestone every this many floors, for the first player to it each event.

milestoneGems.doc: What a milestone pays its first.

rankGems.doc: What each final place pays, first to sixth.

botFloorChance.doc: The chance a stand-in rival clears a floor with each move while it is open.

preciousEvery.doc: Every this many floors, a floor also pays a lump of precious material (19 §10.4).

precious.doc: That lump, by the same scale as the floor’s other rewards — mostly the player’s own material.

worldTravel.doc: How long a march takes to leave each hex: the marcher’s own seconds a hex (explorerSecondsPerHex, armySecondsPerHex) times its terrain’s factor times each of its features’ (Docs/features/19-world-map.md §4).

feature.doc: By feature, multiplied in for each the hex holds.

portal.doc: The Portal’s hex, which has no terrain.

worldCamps.doc: Monster camps on the world board: an army on a hex, beaten by each player before they can claim it (Docs/features/19-world-map.md §5.4).

share.doc: The share of hexes on rings 2–6 that carry a camp — never a site, a city or a city’s neighbour. Every inner-ring hex carries one.

lurkingShare.doc: The share of camps that lurk: unseen until the hex is explored.

powerByRing.doc: A camp’s power on rings 1 to 6, the inner ring first.

powerJitter.doc: How far a camp’s power strays from its ring’s, up or down.

creatures.doc: Which creatures hold camps on each kind of ring; one is picked per camp.

goldPerPower.doc: Gold a beaten camp pays, per point of its power.

heroXpPerPower.doc: Hero XP a beaten camp pays, per point of its power.

tributePremium.doc: How much dearer paying a camp off is than the troops it would cost to beat it.

tributeLossShare.doc: The share of a camp’s power a winning army is reckoned to lose to it — what the tribute is priced on.

botHoursPer1000Power.doc: Hours a stand-in rival takes to beat a camp, per 1,000 of its power.

raidHours.doc: How often a camp raids the player’s districts beside it, in hours of UTC — every raid lands at the same hours on every board (19 §5.5).

raidShare.doc: The share of a raided district’s stores the raiders carry off; the district burns.

repairCostShare.doc: What repairing a burnt district costs, as a share of what claiming a district costs now.

repairTimeShare.doc: How long repairing takes, as a share of a district’s build time.

worldScouting.doc: What exploring a hex pays: shown over every misty hex, paid when the explorer sent to it is home (Docs/features/19-world-map.md §3.2).

hoursByRole.doc: Hours of the city’s own production a Gold, Wood, Food or Stone reward pays, by the kind of ring.

rewards.doc: What a hex on each kind of ring may promise; one is rolled per hex, by weight.

weight.doc: How often it is rolled, against the others on the list.

amount.doc: How much it pays — for Gold, Wood, Food and Stone the least it pays, since those are priced in the city’s production; for a pack, how many.

pack.doc: The pack, when the reward is a pack.

weight.doc: How often it is rolled, against the others on the list.

amount.doc: How much it pays — for Gold, Wood, Food and Stone the least it pays, since those are priced in the city’s production; for a pack, how many.

pack.doc: The pack, when the reward is a pack.

amount.doc: How much it pays — for Gold, Wood, Food and Stone the least it pays, since those are priced in the city’s production; for a pack, how many.

pack.doc: The pack, when the reward is a pack.

amount.doc: How much it pays — for Gold, Wood, Food and Stone the least it pays, since those are priced in the city’s production; for a pack, how many.

pack.doc: The pack, when the reward is a pack.

worldPrecious.doc: Precious materials: what a rich hex yields, and the lumps camps and scouting pay (Docs/features/19-world-map.md §7.4).

richFeatureShare.doc: The share of Forest and Mountain hexes that are rich.

richDesertShare.doc: The share of bare Desert hexes that are rich.

perDay.doc: What a rich district yields a day of its wedge’s material — the inner ring multiplies it.

storeDays.doc: How many days of yield its precious store holds.

ownShare.doc: How often a camp’s or a scouting lump is the player’s own material; otherwise one of the other two.

campPerPower.doc: Precious material a beaten camp pays, per point of its power.

worldExchange.doc: The Exchange: offers of one precious material for another between the players of a board (Docs/features/19-world-map.md §7.5).

offerHours.doc: How long an offer stands before it comes back to whoever made it.

maxOffers.doc: How many offers a player may have standing at once.

botTakeHours.doc: How long a stand-in rival takes to take a fair offer of the material it yields.

botOfferAmount.doc: How much of its own material a stand-in rival offers, one for one.
